fields.description: batter-outbound-http read_body (observed at 1630fe8d3f9b51b75417396bbd97478d4167b806, unchanged on master dd1ed7c1) accumulates response bytes in an ordinary Vec, grows it with reserve_exact, shrinks it with shrink_to_fit, drops partial bodies unwiped on size-limit failure, transport failure, cancellation, deadline expiry and exchange drop, and returns Body::Complete(Bytes::from(buffer)) with no zeroizing owner. Response bodies can carry bearer tokens and personal data, and a consumer cannot wipe partial buffers or allocations the transport has already released. data.text: Design at 8853aa3c. Private ZeroizingBuffer (src/send/buffer.rs) owns one fixed Box<[u8]> at a time; its Drop zeroes the whole allocation, and with no reserve or shrink available, Drop is the only release path. Growth and the final fit build a replacement and assign over the old buffer. read_body keeps its growth policy, limit check, 1 MiB preallocation cap and select precedence. Body::Complete(Bytes) is preserved through Bytes::from_owner. Rejected: Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> (a reallocating Vec can release populated storage unwiped). Kept a protected final fit so a returned Bytes still retains exactly its length, as the old shrink_to_fit did; it copies only when capacity differs from length. Inspected resolved sources: bytes 1.12.1 owned vtable (last release drops the owner once; owned_is_unique is false; Vec/BytesMut conversion deep-copies) and zeroize 1.9.1 (volatile write per element). Public items are unchanged; zeroize is private and already in the normal graph through rustls; no Batter dependency added. ADR-010 review recorded in docs/evidence/api-assessments/http.md. Test instrumentation: cfg(test) probe called from the destructor between the wipe and deallocation, reading only live initialized memory. Ablations (Linux, focused lib tests): 13 of 13 protections removed one at a time were caught by the matching tests; restored tree passed. Release-build cost on Linux x86-64: zeroize 0.26 ms/1 MiB, 2.1 ms/8 MiB, 18 ms/64 MiB, synchronous on the releasing thread. Consumer note: Vec::from(bytes) was previously able to reclaim a unique allocation and now always copies, so a caller wrapping that Vec in its own zeroizing owner stays correct at the cost of one extra bounded copy.

Final commit 03076b228ecee20f6947e4f4e9d2c2ac4617438c, PR https://github.com/bpcakes/batter/pull/110. Supersedes the design note above on one point: the protected final fit was removed. A fresh independent review of 8853aa3c found no path that releases owned storage unwiped and no change to preserved transport behaviour, but showed the fit copies and wipes the whole body in the exchange's last poll, about 54 ms for a 60 MiB body by our own measurements, which can exceed RESERVE to reclaim less than half of an allocation. A completed body now keeps the allocation it grew into, at most twice its length and never above the limit (unit-tested). One growth step has the same synchronous cost, now disclosed in the deadline limits and on RESERVE: about 56 ms for 64 MiB. Review also corrected: a uniqueness claim tested only with a live clone (now tested on the sole handle), release-order wording (all six orders now executed), whole-allocation wording (tail dirtied so the wipe is distinguishable), a changelog line that understated the try_into_mut behaviour change, an architecture paragraph order and a hyper citation. fields.description:
Same mechanism as the batter-70qx cleanup fix, on the admission path. runlimit-postgres/src/gcra.rs run_transaction computes one evaluation instant now = max(database sample, every locked shard's observed_at_ms) and UPDATE_WATERMARKS writes it to every shard in the batch. After a clock regression leaves one shard's watermark ahead, a check_all spanning that shard and another evaluates the other shard's keys at the advanced instant (early replenishment) and permanently advances that shard's clock.

Executed evidence (temporary experiment, PostgreSQL 18.6, 2026-11-10, not committed): policy 1 per 60 s; a shard-1 key consumed and then denied alone; shard 0 watermark set to start+120 s. A single check of the shard-1 key was denied (alone=false), but check_all([shard-0 key, shard-1 key]) was allowed (batch=true), and both shard clocks became start+120 s.

Decision needed: keep one batch evaluation instant (documented single-instant batch semantics, memory parity), or evaluate each check at max(sample, its own shard watermark) and persist per-shard watermarks. Without a clock regression the two are identical. Related: batter-ctk7.2 owns GCRA batch preflight/commit shape.
fields.title: GCRA check_all evaluates and persists every batch shard at the most advanced shard's watermark

Independent confirmation of the four runtime defects (session 5f34af7e, 2026-11-10), each by reverting only the source fix hunk and running its new test on Rust 1.98.1:
- Axum plain registration: plain_server_builds_application_layers_once_across_connections failed with [5, 6, 7] vs [5, 5, 5]; passes with the fix; peer variant passes either way. Root cause confirmed in axum-0.8.9 routing/mod.rs: Service<IncomingStream> for Router<()> returns self.clone().with_state(()) per connection. Consequence: tower ConcurrencyLimitLayer::layer creates a new semaphore, so a Router::layer limit over handler routes was per connection.
- Empty supervisor: a_service_that_registers_nothing_never_reports_ready panicked 'an empty supervisor reported readiness' without the fix (ReadinessProgress latched Ready before drain).

- TUI status line: a_fetch_error_is_shown_even_after_an_earlier_notice failed without the fix. The line was already styled red from last_error while printing the notice.

Additional changes:
- batter-runlimit PreparedHttp::in_process TestClient served an unprepared Router, rebuilding layers on every request. New test in_process_client_builds_application_layers_once_across_requests failed [5, 6, 7] before; it now uses with_state(()) once, like the served connect-info path. All 41 http tests pass.
- batter-core lifecycle: start_driver now makes the only emptiness decision and returns Some(EmptySupervisor), which wait_for_shutdown honors, so a second predicate cannot drift.

fields.description: Two confirmed deadlocks in runledger-postgres workflow persistence. (A) Job terminal completion takes the workflow_runs row FOR SHARE when releasing a ready dependent (release.rs workflow_run_allows_step_release_tx) and FOR UPDATE later in recompute_workflow_run_status_tx; two disjoint branches completing together both hold FOR SHARE and both request FOR UPDATE (reproduced on PostgreSQL 18: 35 of 40 iterations deadlocked). The worker does not retry, so the reaper re-runs or dead-letters an already-succeeded job. (B) Steps are inserted in builder order with uuidv7 ids and forward references are allowed, so a dependent declared before its prerequisite has a smaller id. Job completion locks prerequisite P then dependents; external completion, append, list-for-update and cancel lock all steps in id order, so the whole-run locker holds D and waits on P while completion holds P and waits on D (reproduced with a gated test). Fix: every multi-step workflow mutation takes the workflow_runs row FOR UPDATE before any workflow_steps row.

data.text: Implemented (uncommitted, branch fix/audit-runtime-defects): every multi-step workflow mutation takes the workflow_runs row FOR UPDATE before any workflow_steps row. New crate-private proof WorkflowRunRowLock (locking.rs) is produced only by lock_workflow_run_row_tx / lock_workflow_run_for_update_tx and required by lock_workflow_step_rows_for_update_tx, lock_workflow_steps_for_update_tx, the terminal step lock, release_candidate_step_tx, enqueue_root_steps_tx, resolve_terminal_step_queue_tx and recompute_workflow_run_status_tx. Orders: job completion = job row -> shared release lock -> run -> steps (unlocked read of the immutable run id first); external completion and append = run -> steps -> release try-lock; cancel = jobs -> exclusive lock -> jobs -> run -> steps; enqueue locks its new run before root release. No SQL text of checked queries changed (.sqlx untouched); append.rs stays at its 836-line ceiling. Tests: runledger-postgres/tests/workflow_lock_order.rs, two gated deterministic cases (run-row FOR KEY SHARE gate for disjoint branches; release-lock gate with dependent declared first). Both FAILED on the original source (40P01 in 'lock workflow run for status recompute' and 'lock workflow step rows for mutation') and pass with the fix. Full runledger-postgres suite: 60 binaries, 490 passed, 0 failed (Docker postgres:18). Clippy -D warnings clean with and without --all-features. Docs: CHANGELOG (incl. rolling-upgrade caveat), README workflow DAG note, runledger-postgres AGENTS invariant. Pending: full scripts/verify.sh on the integrated tree.

Implemented in an isolated worktree and applied to the main tree (uncommitted). Log sites: 5 panic-payload fields removed (dead_letter.rs notify_handler_of_dead_letter, observer.rs notify_observer, reaper/terminal_hooks.rs warn_panicked + warn_panicked_hook_missing_metadata, reaper/observers.rs log_reaped_observer_panic); 18 JoinError sites now log task_id/is_panic/is_cancelled (worker.rs x2, worker/observers.rs x8, reaper/terminal_hooks.rs x6, reaper/observers.rs x2). Event messages unchanged. RuntimeShutdownFailure moved to settlement/report/failure.rs (re-exported at the same path) with manual Display (byte-identical, tested) and Error impl: source() is None for LoopJoin/DescendantJoin, Signal and LoopInvalidConfig keep sources. Shared test log capture in src/test_logs.rs. Tests: 9 log-capture tests with String and &'static str sentinels (all failed when production log hunks were reverse-applied: 54/54 site checks leaked) plus 3 source-chain/Display tests (chain test failed against the original thiserror enum). Docs: runledger CHANGELOG 'Callback panic diagnostics', downstream-agent-guide contradiction fixed, docs/operations.md and docs/guarantees.md stale statements corrected. Agent checks: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test -p runledger-runtime 525 passed 0 failed, file budget exit 0. Pending: verify.sh on the integrated tree.

fields.description: Inferred from code, not reproduced. mark_workflow_step_running_for_claim_tx (runledger-postgres/src/jobs/workflows/runtime/claim_transitions.rs ~14-26) runs UPDATE workflow_steps WHERE job_id = ANY(...) for a claimed job batch, locking several step rows of possibly one run in index/physical order without the workflow-run row. Whole-run lockers (external completion, append, list-for-update, cancel) now hold the run row and lock steps in id order, so a claim holding step Sb and waiting on Sa can cycle with a locker holding Sa and waiting on Sb when job-id order differs from step-id order. Fix candidate: lock the batch's steps ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE before the UPDATE; add a gated test.

fields.description: Verified on PostgreSQL 18.6 by a reviewer: when a job row is released after cancellation's first job-lock pass, job completion holds that job row and waits on the shared release lock while cancellation holds the exclusive lock and waits on the job row. The deadlock detector (1 s) fires before the 5 s release-lock cap, so the error is 40P01, not workflow.release_conflict; is_release_lock_timeout_error (locking.rs) maps only 55P03/57014. Decide whether to map 40P01 during that wait, retry, or document.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded; gated test pins the resulting error code and worker handling.

fields.description: Backstop proposed during the lock-order fix but not implemented because runledger-postgres error.rs states 'Neither a kind nor its SQLSTATE authorizes replay' and the root guide requires caller-authorized replay. A rolled-back completion transaction is safe to re-run (lease predicate rechecks ownership; observers run only after Ok); CommitUnconfirmed must never be retried even though it exposes sqlstate(). Needs an owner decision recording a policy exception before any implementation.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Owner decision recorded; if accepted, retry lives in owned completion wrappers, matches only QueryError 40P01/40001, has tests for retry, no-retry on CommitUnconfirmed and lease mismatch after expiry.

fields.description: Inferred from code: reap_expired_lease_batch locks up to limit expired jobs across runs (SKIP LOCKED, lease order) and handles them one by one in one transaction with savepoints; each workflow job completion now holds its run row until commit. Two reapers, or a reaper and a whole-run locker, can hold run rows in different orders. Savepoint deferral bounds the damage but the other party can be the victim. Consider grouping rows by run or committing per run.

data.text: Verification (2026-11-10, integrated tree with batter-70qx.2/.3/.4): bash scripts/verify.sh exit 0 on Rust 1.98.1 (fmt, file budgets, four Clippy configurations, all six matrix parts with every subprocess status 0: 4671 passed, 0 failed, 438 ignored; rustdoc; all HTTP smoke profiles PASS). Earlier attempts: run 1 failed on pre-existing load-sensitive workflow_results final-probe tests (filed batter-70qx.10; stress shows 3/20 failures on the original source vs 1/20 with the change); run 2 exposed a real interaction, runledger-runtime external_completion_conflicts_when_cancel_waits_on_step_rows, which hand-held step rows without the run row (the old external-completion order) so cancel became a deadlock victim; replaced by tests/workflow_run_row_lock_order.rs (holds run row then steps, waits on the new runledger:lock_workflow_run_row marker, still asserts workflow.release_conflict and clean cancel); runs 3-4 failed batter-core command_signals only because my detached launcher inherited SIG_IGN for SIGINT (SigIgn 0x7; the test documents this); run 5 restored default dispositions (SigIgn 0) and passed. Follow-up change in this item: lock_workflow_run_for_update_tx (cancel, append, list-for-update) now acquires through lock_workflow_run_row_tx so its wait carries the runledger:lock_workflow_run_row marker; its checked status query re-locks the held row (no SQL text change). runledger-runtime suite 550 passed, runledger-postgres --all-features 494 passed after it.

Implemented in an isolated worktree, reviewed and applied (uncommitted). Scheduler: committed full batch re-polls after yield + shutdown check; otherwise waits min(poll, max(500 ms, earliest active next_fire_at - now)); errors wait the full poll interval. Reaper: continues only when processed > 0, processed + deferred >= limit and reaped-observer owner below its 64 cap; shutdown checked between passes, never raced. New pub runledger_postgres::jobs::earliest_active_schedule_fire_at (non-macro query, rustdoc + no_run example, covered by ScheduledDispatch grants). Capped (1000) dropped-occurrence warning after commit. Docs: README, downstream guide (lag and jitter skip disclosed), runtime AGENTS, CHANGELOG. Tests: tests/scheduler_loop.rs, tests/reaper_drain.rs, runledger-postgres tests/schedule_earliest_fire.rs, unit tests in scheduler/wait.rs, scheduler/coalescing, reaper/cadence.rs; drain and shutdown tests fail by timeout on the original loop; no-hot-loop tests fail against targeted mutations (Err->immediate 782-890 vs 2 passes; no deferral 627 vs 3; dropped processed>0 guard 348 vs 3).

fields.title: Repair panel findings in reaper workflow locking and cadence regressions

data.text: Implemented batch-wide workflow-run preparation before reaper row mutations, with sorted deduplicated runs, per-run preparation savepoints, NOWAIT row acquisition and bounded advisory/table waits. Successful locks live outside row savepoints; failed preparation defers only associated jobs and never reattempts after step mutation. Direct-only jobs keep their existing grants; the batch still commits once. Live PostgreSQL regressions: mixed retry/terminal and unstarted/terminal tests failed on the pre-repair code with SQLSTATE 40P01, then passed with the repair. Current workflow_lock_order suite passed 8/8, including busy-run isolation, rollback lock retention, opposite-expiry competing reapers and DirectJobExecution role. Scheduler real-loop partial-pass wake regression passed. Full verification and fresh panel reviews pending. Documentation now limits the completion/reaper ordering claim: existing bulk claim transitions remain outside it; no universal deadlock-freedom claim. Logs: /tmp/batter-panel-review-fU8I9RpZ.

Mutation checks executed and restored: forcing the scheduler partial-pass branch to sleep the full polling interval compiled and failed the new wake regression (target never fired before the test deadline); inserting the old early step-row acquisition compiled and failed the strengthened inverted-step regression with SQLSTATE 40P01. Initial scheduler mutation caused dead-code compilation errors and was discarded; the recorded behavioral run keeps the helper referenced and fails at the intended assertion. Savepoint recovery now retains the operation error if rollback or release fails. Full controller validation starts after formatting.

Required verify round 1 passed formatting and file budgets, then stopped on Clippy cognitive_complexity in the new mixed_batch test helper (35/20). Split fixture enqueue/claim/expiry setup and gate/concurrency choreography into focused private test helpers; all synchronization and outcome assertions remain. Focused all-features Clippy for workflow_lock_order now passes with no lint allowance. Controller repair round 2 submitted; complete verify rerunning. No code commit or staging.

Controller round 2 required validation passed: bash scripts/verify.sh on Rust 1.98.1, Linux; formatting, file budgets, all four Clippy configurations, all six test-matrix parts, rustdoc and five HTTP smoke profiles completed. Exact receipt/log: .git/jig/review-fix/5a283a66-2971-40e6-ba79-f0c55086a5f7/assignments/00009-validate. Fresh independent Claude and Codex review assignments 00010-review and 00011-review are running against the verified combined working tree. No repeat of the passed matrix is planned absent new changes or findings.
